title: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies - National Values Education - Preventing Drug Trafficking
exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When a convicted drug trafficker is legally forced by the government to give up their houses, cars, and bank accounts purchased with drug money, it is known as:
questions.explain: **Forfeiture of assets** is a severe legal consequence where the government seizes all wealth, properties, and accounts (both local and foreign) linked to illicit drug proceeds.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: To systematically prevent drug trafficking at the grassroots level, governments often introduce scholarship schemes, vocational loans, and job creation programs. This preventive measure is termed:
questions.explain: Since poverty is a major driver of trafficking, **alleviation of poverty** through economic empowerment reduces the financial desperation that cartels exploit.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: The establishment of specialized law enforcement agencies like the NDLEA (National Drug Law Enforcement Agency) in Nigeria falls directly under which preventive measure?
questions.explain: **Legislation** involves the government enacting laws to prohibit trafficking and creating specialized statutory agencies (like the NDLEA) to hunt down, arrest, and prosecute offenders.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Why is the intervention of the **International Community** critical in the prevention of drug trafficking?
options: Because drug trafficking is a transnational crime requiring global cooperation, intelligence sharing, and extradition treaties to dismantle cartels across borders
Because local police are not allowed to arrest any citizen
Because all drug proceeds must legally be paid to the United Nations
Because drugs are only manufactured in outer space
questions.explain: Drug cartels operate globally. The **International Community** (e.g., INTERPOL, UNODC) must collaborate to track shipments, share security intelligence, and extradite criminals across borders.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q:

Based on the syllabus and the diagram illustrating a counter-measure to 'Ignorance', what is the most appropriate preventive measure for 'Prevention X'?
questions.explain: The direct cure for ignorance in the syllabus's preventative framework is **Education**. Through widespread enlightenment and schooling, individuals learn about the dire consequences of trafficking.

questions.q: If a government decides to confiscate the foreign bank accounts of a convicted drug baron in Europe with the help of foreign authorities, this combines which two preventive/consequence elements?
options: Forfeiture of assets and International Community
Constructive use of time and Good friends
questions.explain: Seizing accounts involves the **forfeiture of assets (foreign)**, which can only be successfully executed through treaties and cooperation with the **International Community**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: The international tool used by the International Community to track and arrest drug traffickers who flee from one country to another is:
options: INTERPOL (International Criminal Police Organization) and Extradition Treaties
questions.explain: **INTERPOL** and **Extradition Treaties** are the primary international mechanisms that allow nations to collaborate, track fugitives, and legally transfer traffickers back to face prosecution.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Examine the role of the government in drug trafficking prevention. While *legislation* passes the laws, what handles the physical arrest, intelligence gathering, and drug confiscation?
questions.explain: **Law enforcement agencies** are strictly tasked with the executive duties of gathering intelligence, executing arrests, and confiscating illegal substances on behalf of the state.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: A comprehensive national strategy mapped to eliminate drug trafficking incorporates $E+L+A+I$. If $E=$ Education, $L=$ Legislation, and $I=$ International Community, what does $A$ stand for according to the syllabus?
questions.explain: The prevention parameters taught are Education, Legislation, **Alleviation of poverty ($A$)**, and International Community support.
